===================================================
  Open An Interactive Job on Hopper GPU Node
===================================================
 To run short interactive AI and/or Deep Learning jobs meant for debugging of code on GPU,
 Following the below 3 Steps.

 Step 1:  Launch a login session on GPU system by entering the below command:

   [hopper-l-01]> [1;32mqsub -I -P Project-Name -l select=1:ngpus=1 -l walltime=01:00:00 [0m

   where 
         -I                  :  Launch in interactive session
         -P Project-Name     :  Set to use project < Project-Name, e.g. CFP01-CF-nnn > 
         -l select=1:ngpus=1 :  Request for 1 GPU ONLY for the session
         -l walltime=**      :  Request walltime max up to 2 hours

   The default walltime for such session is 1 hour, and max to be 2 hours.

 Step 2:  Open Singularity container on Hopper (GPU) Server by:

   [hopper-0X]> [1;32mmodule load singularity [0m
   [hopper-0X]> [1;32msingularity exec -e /app1/common/singularity-img/hopper/pytorch/pytorch_2.3.0_cuda_12.4_ngc_24.04.sif bash [0m

   You can list other AI/DL containers in folder < /app1/common/singularity-img/hopper/ >. 

 Step 3:  Start and run your AI/DL python program:

   # [1;32mpython cifar10_resnet.py [0m

hpc pbs.stdout:
1, Prepare your job submission script first. You can list out the sample job script as blow command,
   and then copy and edit the sample script to save as yours, e.g. myjob1.txt. You can use vi or nano editor.
[1;32m   #>  hpc ai [0m

2, Submit the job as:
[1;32m   #>  qsub  myjob1.txt [0m

   If pbs commands qsub, qstat, ..., are not available, enter "module load pbs" first.
[1;32m   #>  module load pbs [0m


3, Check status of job by command:
[1;32m   #>  qstat        ## list current jobs in simple format [0m
[1;32m   #>  qstat -aw    ## list current jobs in wider  format [0m
[1;32m   #>  qstat -ans1  ## list current jobs in detailed format [0m
[1;32m   #>  qstat -q     ## list out queues [0m
[1;32m   #>  qstat -H     ## list out finished jobs [0m
[1;32m   #>  qstat -x     ## list out finished and current jobs [0m
[1;32m   #>  qstat -f jobid  ## list out full info of a job [0m

[1;32m   #>  qgpu_smi   jobid  ## check the usage of GPUs and CPUs of a running job. [0m
[1;32m   #>  inspectjob jobid  ## check the average usage of GPUs and CPUs of a running job. [0m

4, To terminate a job:
[1;32m   #>  qdel jobid          ## to terminate a job gracefully. [0m

5, To list out available job queues and the loading status:
[1;32m   #>  qstat -q [-Q] [0m
[1;32m   #>  gstat [0m
